highlights.title: Leclerc takes blame for Hamilton clash at Monza after Ferrari talks
highlights.summary: Charles Leclerc has admitted "I didn't behave the way I should have" when racing Ferrari team-mate Lewis Hamilton at the opening lap of the Italian Grand Prix.
body: Hamilton accused the team of having "no rules" after he was forced wide by Leclerc at the exit of the first chicane, an incident which cost him six positions, and could only recover to sixth place at Ferrari's home event.
Ahead of this weekend's Spanish Grand Prix in Madrid, both drivers discussed the incident with Ferrari chairman John Elkann, chief executive Benedetto Vigna and team principal Frederic Vasseur.

"What was very important was to speak first of all. It's been quite a few years now that I've been in Ferrari and I know how it feels when everything on Ferrari is kind of on fire and if you don't speak between Lewis and I, you can get caught with this noise around the team," said Leclerc.

"It's not that there's no reason for that noise but the intensity of the noise is a bit too crazy. When you look at Monza, there has been friction between other team-mates and we barely talk about it but when it's about Ferrari, it takes proportion that is not normal.
points: Charles Leclerc has admitted "I didn't behave the way I should have" when racing Ferrari team-mate Lewis Hamilton at the opening lap of the Italian Grand Prix.

highlights.title: Sure, Meta’s AI Muse works, but it sure creeps me out
highlights.summary: Meta has launched its new Muse assistant, marking the company's first real foray into AI-powered productivity tools. The company says its AI agent can "take the busywork off your plate" by helping you with online shopping, emails, trip-planning, and more.
body: One of the first tasks I assigned Muse, which carries out actions using a cloud-based virtual computer, was to sort through my Gmail inbox and delete messages I don’t need. That required me to connect Muse to my Google account and give it permission to access, read, and delete emails. The process didn’t go smoothly on mobile; the Google sign-in screen kept glitching and returning me to the Muse website instead of the app. I eventually got it working on my laptop, where it deleted thousands of promotional emails and updates. I didn’t feel good about permitting Muse to view all of my emails given Meta’s track record on privacy over the years.

highlights.title: Nintendo of America thanks fans for dealing with tariff-related price hikes by encouraging them to spend more money in a new sale
highlights.summary: Nintendo of America is currently facing a class action lawsuit for refusing to pass tariff refunds onto customers, and it's against that backdrop it today announced a "Customer Appreciation Sale" apparently made possible by those rebates.
body: In a blog post, Nintendo called this one of its "largest promotions ever", and included the following line which has had people scratching their heads: "While Nintendo absorbed most tariff-related costs, the refunds helped make promotions like this one possible."

A quick recap: following the introduction of tariffs by the current US government last year, Nintendo increased the price of multiple products in the country, citing "market conditions" as justification.

Nintendo, in this sale announcement, argues that it "absorbed" most of the costs, but the company has received a refund. The US consumers who bought Nintendo products since the price increase also suffered increased costs thanks to the tariffs, but they aren't receiving refunds. The reason this is rubbing people the wrong way is because Nintendo is thanking them for dealing with increased costs by encouraging them to spend more money.

The counter argument is, hey, why look a gift horse in the mouth? This is a discount on some games and peripherals at a time when buying new stuff in this market is awfully expensive. This ultimately could be seen as a gesture of goodwill, and one Switch owners could benefit from.

highlights.title: September’s Collabs Corner: Raiding John Cena in Clash of Clans, Among Us in Subway Surfers, and more
highlights.summary: Among the updates, announcements and marketing drives for mobile games, this bustling industry sees a never-ending flow of crossovers and collaborations. Some partnerships see characters from one game IP enter another. Others see brands or logos show up in unexpected places.
body: With so many games and so many crossovers, it can be hard to keep track. So, here’s a roundup of all the latest collaborations happening on mobile.

Supercell’s Clash of Clans has formed its second tag team with the WWE, bringing six wrestling stars in-game as playable characters. Among them are Cody Rhodes as Barbarian King, The Undertaker as Grand Warden and Alexa Bliss as Archer Queen.

The collaboration sees players join Cody Rhodes on the hunt for John Cena’s in-game village, unlocking exclusive rewards as they seek out his base this month. The more players raid, the higher the chance of locating the elusive locale. There’s even a Cody Rhodes statue to be found.
John Cena, the wrestling giant turned actor, is said to be a long-time player of Clash of Clans.

There will be seven Premier League matches on Boxing Day this year, with Hull City vs Liverpool - kicking off at 5.30pm - and Newcastle vs Man City - kicking off at 8pm - featuring as a live Sky Sports double header.

A triple header on Sky Sports then follows on Super Sunday on December 27, with Frank Lampard taking on Chelsea as Coventry boss at 2pm. That match is then followed by Manchester United vs Nottingham Forest at 4.30pm, then Crystal Palace vs Arsenal at 7pm.

highlights.title: Mathematicians want proof OpenAI didn’t use their work
highlights.summary: Another researcher is challenging OpenAI about the data driving its increasingly impressive array of mathematical discoveries. Just days after a bitter row erupted over whether the company's models benefited from unpublished work, a second mathematician has come forward accusing the AI giant of…
body: In a series of posts on Mastodon, mathematician Andreas Thom raised concerns that interactions he and his colleagues had had with the ChatGPT chatbot before OpenAI’s triumphant announcement may have contributed to its success in the field. One of the 10 results OpenAI announced with great fanfare last month involved Thom’s area of expertise, so-called non-sofic groups, and OpenAI acknowledged that their result built heavily on previous work by Thom and fellow mathematician Gábor Kun.

Thom said he began reflecting on his own interactions with OpenAI after Tristan Buckmaster, a mathematics professor at New York University, publicly questioned whether the company’s AI models had benefited from his use of OpenAI’s Codex. After OpenAI announced its non-sofic groups result, it was widely criticized in mathematical circles for failing to acknowledge recent contributions from Thom and Kun and the company quietly amended its writeup. Non-sofic groups are, roughly speaking, infinite mathematical structures that cannot be approximated by finite ones.

highlights.title: August 2026 mobile game charts: Fate/Grand Order’s big anniversary, Valorant Mobile's rise and Brawl Stars’ worst month of the year
highlights.summary: Below you can see the latest top games and companies by downloads and revenue for August 2026, as well as the big stories and trends from the last month. Data is provided by AppMagic. Check out profiles of the world's top publishers in the Top 50 Mobile Game Makers 2025 list.
body: Note that these estimates are based on gross revenue from player spending across the App Store and Google Play only. It does not feature estimates from alternative marketplaces or direct-to-consumer platforms.

Aniplex’s long-running gacha Fate/Grand Order has seen player spending spike to its highest monthly sum of the year. The game made $57.7 million this August with an anniversary celebration in Japan, more than doubling July’s $22.5m.

In fact, this was the anime-style RPG’s best month since last August. The game makes 89% of its earnings from Japan, meaning the month is a major one each year - more than the North American anniversary in early July.

On a daily spending basis, earnings reached their highest in more than five years this August. Fate/Grand Order generated $4.6m on the 15th, surpassing any daily record from the past five anniversaries but not quite matching the game’s lifetime high of $5.6m on January 1st, 2021.

highlights.title: ‘NAZA’ Review: A Sober and Indispensable Doc Highlights the Immoral, State-of-the-Art Killing Machine Employed by the IDF in Gaza
highlights.summary: The Guardian served as producer, and Jonathan Glazer as executive producer, on this exposé by Yuval Abraham and Rachel Szor, part of the directing team behind 2024 Oscar winner 'No Other Land.'
body: It’s hard to describe all of the feelings provoked by watching a film like Yuval Abraham and Rachel Szor’s NAZA. Outrage for sure. Indignity as well. Most certainly disgust, on a profound level, for the current Israeli regime and its prime minister, Bibi Netanyahu.

That’s clearly not the purpose of this brave and indispensable movie, which deserves to enter the historical record in the same way as Claude Lanzmann’s Shoah, an excerpt of which we see playing on a screen outside the Tel Aviv Cinematheque. Both works bear witness to acts of genocide — this is the term employed by an IDF officer in the film — and both use a rigorous interview process to get people to speak of the unspeakable, the main difference being that NAZA focuses exclusively on the perpetrators instead of the victims.

highlights.title: Charlie Kirk Was Shot a Year Ago. The Conspiracy Theories Are More Rampant Than Ever
highlights.summary: Experts say conspiracy theorizing about the identity and motive of Charlie Kirk’s killer will likely continue for a long time to come.
body: In the days after the assassination of conservative activist and Turning Point cofounder Charlie Kirk, the online reaction was a mess. Graphic videos of the shooting were everywhere within minutes of his death, far-right figures called for violence and vengeance, and right-wing lawmakers and influencers called for the cancellation —and worse—of anyone celebrating. Then, the conspiracy theories began.

It’s been one year since Kirk’s death, and conspiracy theories about the shooting have persisted, supercharged by social media algorithms and right-wing influencers like Candace Owens, who has used her huge following to push baseless allegations about the incident.

Experts believe these conspiracy theories will continue for a long time to come. “There’s no reason to believe conspiracy theories about Kirk’s murder will lose steam anytime soon,” Jared Holt, senior researcher at Open Measures, tells WIRED. “If anything, I expect them to escalate further as the criminal trial against Tyler Robinson, the man accused of killing Kirk, plays out over the next year or so. The trial is bound to draw major media attention and offer conspiracy theorists a source of new material to work from.”

highlights.title: Powering AI is an architecture problem
highlights.summary: On July 22, 2026, a transmission line fault in Ashburn, Virginia—the heart of the world’s largest data center cluster—knocked more than 3 gigawatts of load off the grid in seconds. And it wasn’t the first time.
body: The AI power debate is mostly about generation: more turbines, more solar, more transmission. The grid needs more electrons. But the outages in Virginia weren’t supply failures; they were architecture failures. And a giant wave of interconnections is arriving on that same architecture, putting grid reliability at risk. It’s a problem nobody wants to own.

The grid was built around predictable loads: steel mills, refineries, and houses at dinnertime. Different load sizes, same process—drawing power smoothly, misbehaving occasionally, and recovering gracefully.

An AI campus can swing 70% of its load in milliseconds during a training run, then trip offline just as fast at the first sign of trouble upstream to protect billions in compute. Each is rational alone. Together, at gigawatt scale, they’re a problem the grid has never solved—and the next wave of data center campuses is planned at exactly that scale.

The standard data center power stack hasn’t changed in decades. Medium-voltage power arrives, transformers step it down, low-voltage uninterruptible power supply (UPS) units condition it, and it reaches the racks. Push that design to AI scale, and it cracks in three places.

highlights.summary: Magic: The Gathering ’s upcoming set Reality Fracture is the culmination of a three-year plot arc and the 19-year story of Jace Beleren, the mind mage who has become one of the game’s most iconic characters.
body: Francis Tneh illustrated the Booster Fun version of the blue sorcery Cruel Calculations with a new frame called Sculptor’s Stronghold, which will appear on a total of 25 cards in the set. Executive producer Mike Turian tells Polygon the treatment is meant to demonstrate how Jace is watching over the Echoverse. The card is closely tied to the Theorix school at Hexhaven, the Echoverse’s twisted version of Strixhaven, which the Theorist uses as his base.

“This art for Cruel Calculations shows some of the inherent risks that come with the kind of forbidden reality-bending math and physics being taught in Theorix,” Reality Fracture narrative lead Meris Mullaley tells Polygon via email. “The best Theorix students can learn to bend reality, but for every elite student, there are many peers who failed their tests.”
The card is meant to synergize with Omit Variables, a prepared spell found on Theorix cards like the uncommon Paradox Shaper, which mills three cards for one black or blue mana.

body: Taking place on September 14th, 2026 in Bratislava, PixelCon is a free, open conference aimed at game developers, students, indie creators and professionals from across the games industry. Registration is required due to limited capacity.

Among the international speakers is Jeremy Widdowson, head of growth at Rovio, bringing experience from one of Europe's best-known mobile games companies, the studio behind the global Angry Birds franchise.

The programme also features Stanislav Stankovič, game design director at Electronic Arts, Maya Hofree, general manager of Hay Day at Supercell, and Florian Blaesche, director of player experience at Wooga, who will share their perspectives on building successful mobile games, player engagement and long-term retention.
The international line-up will be joined by Slovak and Czech industry leaders, including Pixel Federation experts and founders of local studios such as Flyboys, PowerPlay Studio and Impact Games.

highlights.title: Ralph Lauren proves the American dream still sells at New York fashion week
highlights.summary: Designer mixes burnt-out velvet and shredded denim with a mythology that keeps getting more profitable. The opening show of fashion’s month of catwalks was not on the official schedule, but Viola Davis and Cynthia Erivo were snuggled on to celebrity-packed benches in a cathedral-sized marble hall…
body: Ralph Lauren, 86, took his bow at the end of this women’s wear show casually dressed in a varsity jacket spelling out New York. In an industry obsessed with youth and novelty, Lauren is more relevant than ever in his ninth decade.

He described the show as “irreverent”. Velvet evening wear was burnt out to show a little skin beneath. There were shredded, low-slung jeans – take note, jeans-wearers everywhere – and a wink to the extra-wide ties that started his empire 59 years ago.
The spray-painted brocade gowns and lush embroidered evening coats on this catwalk will be giddily expensive, but the energy propelling the brand comes from a much broader audience.

Gen Z has rediscovered Ralph Lauren, and its Polo shirts, rugby shirts and baseball caps are cool again, a renaissance that shows up emphatically on the balance sheet. This year the fashion house reached its highest ever annual revenue figure of $8.1bn (£6bn) – a rise of 15% on the previous year.

highlights.title: AI agents are flooding public services with new requests
highlights.summary: “The vast majority of cases we find are people who are entitled to claim for something, claiming for that thing,” the researcher told TechCrunch.
body: As AI makes it easier to fill forms and file complaints, public services around the world are seeing enormous jumps in applications and other requests.

In the United Kingdom, complaints to the housing ombudsman more than doubled since the introduction of ChatGPT, rising from 2600 in 2022 to just over 7,000 last year. The United States’ Consumer Financial Protection Bureau (CFPB) saw 5x growth in complaints over the same period. There were similar jumps in Brazilian judicial petitions and German parliamentary petitions.

Researcher Chris Schmitz is tracking this rise as part of a broader trend he called “agentic flooding.” In a paper set to be presented next month at the AI Ethics and Society conference, he looks at 84 different cases of potential flooding across 11 jurisdictions, finding broad evidence that AI tools are changing the way people interact with public services.

The deed is memorialized in a mural depicting Korra in the Avatar state as a demonic figure.

That’s a big problem for the new Avatar, the Earthbender Pavi, a child even younger than Aang was at the start of his journey. Pavi lives in the city of Ellora, a metropolis tucked between canyons that protect it from constantly raging sandstorms and tornadoes. Kids there grow up learning to hate the Avatar for causing this cataclysm. But when the Airbender Jae is caught under rocks in a sandstorm, Pavi reveals she is the Avatar by using both Earthbending and Airbending.

highlights.title: Maven Robotics wants to steal your robot deployment deal
highlights.summary: Maven Robotics emerged from stealth today with a $100 million Series A and active deployments.
body: In 2024, Maven Robotics was brand new, and they had nothing—”a cartoon of a robot and a team of people,” CEO and co-founder Hamza Derbas told TechCrunch.

Still, they heard a large consumer goods company with logistics needs was in town to meet with four rival robot companies about automation. Derbas talked his way into a meeting with the company and, instead of talking about his views on robots, asked to visit their factories and warehouses.

“We saw how people were working; we zeroed in on flows we could immediately bring value to,” he told TechCrunch. “We showed them that our approach to robotics is different—we’re not trying to solve a single robot problem. We’re trying to autonomously take on the task end to end: It hooks in from one side to a warehouse management system; product goes on trucks on the other side.”

They won the deal, beating out companies with existing robots. After two years of work with that company and a few other partners, Derbas says Maven has as many as eight robots working 16 hours a day, with 99% or higher uptime.

highlights.summary: A clone of Old School RuneScape that appeared on the internet this week, and stoked the ire of the RuneScape community, has quickly been shut down.
body: The clone was made by e OpenAI employee Rohan Varma, who used the GPT-6 Astra to build a version of RuneScape he named Elderwood, which was playable in a browser.

In a video - itself created with gen-AI - uploaded to X, we see a character created and spawning outside Lumbridge castle, with an inventory of bread, coins, and basic tools. We then see the same character fighting giant rats, chopping trees, and equipping steel armour. It looks incredibly similar to Old School RuneScape save for a few inconsistencies..

But as Verma continued to experiment and share their progress on X, the posts caught the attention of the Old School RuneScape community who were displeased with what they found. In a thread posted to the 2007scape Reddit, users were not shy in their criticisms.

"What in the vibe coded shit is this. They even straight up ripped art assets shameless," wrote user RangeCreed. "Love the tweet format. AI bros can only speak in numbers and bullet lists (ideally both at once)," adds Lekamil, while X user Toppo simply summarised the situation with the following: "tl;dr garbage."

highlights.title: Everything New You Can Do With Siri AI
highlights.summary: When iOS 27 arrives, it will bring with it a fully revamped assistant for your iPhone.
body: Siri made its debut on the iPhone in 2011, five years ahead of Google Assistant and 11 years before ChatGPT would open up to the public. Despite the head start, Apple's voice AI has been comprehensively overtaken in recent years, and made to look rather primitive compared to the many generative AI rivals it’s now up against.
With the launch of iOS 27, Apple and Siri are fighting back. There's a new name— Siri AI —and a host of new capabilities that are coming to your iPhone.

These are the new features that you'll be able to make use of once iOS 27 appears on your handset, if you're running the iPhone 15 Pro or iPhone 15 Pro Max or later (including, of course, the iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone Duo ). Only these latest phones have the necessary on-board silicon to meet the higher AI processing demands.

You'll notice when Siri AI arrives that it spends some time indexing everything on your iPhone. That's so it can dig deep into your texts, emails, calendars, and whatever else you have stored on your phone (everything is kept on-device though—nothing gets sent back to Apple).

highlights.title: Unofficial GTA 6 Worldwide Release Times Revealed, And The US Gets It Almost Last
highlights.summary: GTA 6 is one of the most-anticipated games ever, and it arrives on November 19. People naturally want to know when exactly that day it will be available to play, and now it looks the like first indication of that has come to light.
body: GTA Vice scoured PlayStation Store listings for the game across 63 countries and regions, and discovered that the game will not have a global simultaneous release. It looks like the US will be among the last major markets to get it.
Again, this is all based on PlayStation Store listings and is not confirmed by Rockstar. GameSpot has followed up with the developer seeking comment.

According to GTA Vice, GTA 6 will unlock--on the PlayStation Store, at least--at midnight local time. That means people in New Zealand and Australia will get in first and the US will be among the final major regions to get started.

In short, GTA 6 will become available to play in New Zealand at midnight in the country, which works out to 5 AM PT / 8 AM ET on November 18. People in the US will then have to wait 16 hours to play GTA 6 where they live.

body: Kidman’s and Bullock’s characters marvel at the naked 6-foot-5 Pace, and a rollicking comic set-piece begins, as they use their powers to bring him to life. Pace, who’d been cast over Zoom and arrived on set only days before, was suddenly thrashing about nude with two actresses he’d adored from afar — forcing himself to be in the moment despite it all.
